A1.justification: Both PDFs describe REASONING COMPILER. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and expanded evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original compiler speedup experiments on four kernels, with LLM-choice, historical-context, and branching-factor ablations in Section 4 and Appendices B–E.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds a fifth kernel, multiple hardware platforms, end-to-end evaluation, API-cost measurements, and proposal-fallback results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 and Figure 2 revise expansion from applying a proposed transformation sequence to applying one transformation per new node, while retaining the overall LLM–MCTS framework. v2 also specifies rejecting already-present programs. Appendix A still shows multi-transformation proposals, leaving implementation consistency unresolved.

E1.justification: The four original kernels are retained, and v2 adds the Llama-4-Scout MLP kernel and end-to-end Llama-3-8B evaluation. Coverage expands from Intel Core i9 to five target platforms, adding Amazon Graviton2, AMD EPYC 7R13, Apple M2 Pro, and Intel Xeon E3.

E2.justification: The matched kernel comparisons retain TVM MetaSchedule/Evolutionary Search and unguided MCTS. The LLM-choice ablation retains the same six models. Newly cited superoptimization methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds cross-platform and end-to-end evaluation designs. Tables 1–2 compare method-specific sample counts and speedups, with geometric-mean summaries; Section 4.2 introduces speedup per sample alongside the retained comparisons. Appendices F–G add per-experiment API spending and per-expansion fallback measurements. The stated TVM version, exploration constant, and branching factor remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices F–G add focused analyses of API expense and proposal failures across LLMs. The existing LLM-choice, historical-depth, and branching-factor ablations retain their numerical data: v1 Tables 2–4 correspond to v2 Tables 4–6.

E5.justification: Both versions state that each experiment is repeated 20 times and report mean performance. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial kernel, cross-platform, end-to-end, API-cost, and fallback results. For example, Table 3 newly reports 12.74× speedup for Llama-4-Scout at 20 samples. Retained entries also change: Llama-3 MCTS at 144 samples changes from 9.65× to 8.50×, and FLUX convolution MCTS at 36 samples changes from 1.96× to 2.11×. These are reported-value revisions, without evidence establishing why they changed.

T1.justification: Section 2 newly asserts almost-sure asymptotic optimality under finite branching, bounded rewards, and persistent exploration; v1 only described approximate optimization. Section 3.2 also changes the formal tree-edge definition from transformation sequences to individual transformations. No supporting proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claim of sample-efficient, retraining-free LLM-guided MCTS remains. The introduction replaces its earlier empirical headline with 10.8× kernel-level and 5.6× end-to-end sample-efficiency improvements over TVM across five platforms. The conclusion additionally claims energy and training benefits and proposes a self-optimizing LLM cycle.

C2.justification: Appendices F–G add discussion of commercial API dependence, local deployment costs, invalid or performance-regressive proposals, and fallback behavior. Section 4.2 interprets the new results as evidence of portability and end-to-end applicability. The earlier explanations of LLM capacity and historical-context benefits largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A expands the worked prompt and response to include explicit reasoning. v2 identifies additional hardware targets, names Nscale as the Hugging Face API provider, and adds proposal-checking and cost information. The code-access URL and core software and search settings are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction and Section 5 add a focused comparison with enumerative, symbolic, stochastic, hybrid, and neural superoptimization. Additional citations support cost-model use, Llama 4, and performance-improving code edits; the Dally keynote citation is removed. The existing neural-compilation and LLM positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title and author presentation, standardizes terminology, condenses prompt instructions and rollout explanations, rewrites the conclusion, and adds acknowledgments. The main section sequence and most existing exposition and appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, Figure 3 gains a fifth panel, and v1's relative-to-TVM bar chart is removed. The existing ablation plots are retained as renumbered Figure 4. Two main-text comparison tables and two appendix diagnostic tables are added, substantially changing the presentation of evidence.

improvement.justification: The broader hardware and full-model evaluation, together with API-cost and fallback diagnostics, improves assessment of applicability beyond v1's four kernels on one CPU. The gain is tempered by unclear sample-point selection and an unexplained mismatch between v2 Table 1's Intel Core i9 Llama-3 result of 11.0× at 130 samples and Table 3's 8.79× at 144 samples. The new asymptotic-optimality assertion also lacks a supporting proof.
